question: Which chemical element is required to harden steel?
solution:
The correct answer is__** Manganese.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The chemical element required to harden steel is manganese (Mn).
 
• Symbol and Atomic Number: Manganese has the symbol Mn and an atomic number of 25.
 
• Properties: It is a hard, brittle, silvery-white metal and is the second most abundant transition element in the Earth's crust.
 
• Role in Steel Making:
 
 
• Manganese is used in large quantities during the steel-making process.
 
• It improves the strength, workability, and resistance to wear of steel.
 
 
 
• Industrial Uses: Beyond steel, manganese is used in various applications, including:
 
 
• As an oxidizing agent.
 
• In rubber, glass making, and fertilizers.
 
• In ceramics and as a fungicide (manganese sulfate).
 
 
 
• Dietary Element: Manganese is an essential trace element for humans, important for macronutrient metabolism and bone formation, and can be found in various foods such as nuts, grains, legumes, seeds, coffee, tea, oysters, rice, and greens.
 
• Discovery: Manganese was discovered in 1774 by Carl-Wilhelm Scheele and isolated by Johan Gottlieb Gahn in the same year.​

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• ​**Chromium**: Added to steel to enhance hardness and corrosion resistance.
 
• Chromium is a crucial element added to steel to harden and increase its strength.
 
• The addition of chromium forms stainless steel, which has excellent resistance to corrosion and rusting.
 
• Chromium increases the steel’s hardness by forming chromium carbides, which enhance wear resistance.
 
• **Nickel**: Improves the toughness and ductility of steel, often used in combination with chromium in stainless steel.
 
• **Vanadium**: Enhances hardness and strength by forming stable carbides in the steel.
